integrity: The proof expands the two counts into vertex indicators and motif-copy indicators. Only incidences where the vertex belongs to the motif copy contribute covariance; conditioning on that copy forces exactly the motif-degree number of incident edges. The resulting binomial ratio gives the exact formula, and exhaustive rational enumeration independently replays regular and nonregular motifs on small host graphs.
scientific_limitations: The exact formula uses independent-edge Erdős–Rényi sampling.
The one-threshold universality is specific to regular motifs; nonregular motifs combine several internal degree contributions.

A general orthogonal-decomposition treatment of random graph statistics may contain the finite covariance identity implicitly, although the inspected degree-count and triangle-count sources do not state it.
title: Regular motifs share a universal degree-count covariance threshold in Erdős–Rényi graphs
